proposed_profile.name: EasyMesh 6.1 Profile-1 procedure subset for an isolated lab
proposed_profile.rationale: Both WFA documents are accessible publisher editions released on the same date. EasyMesh 6.1 section 2 cites the 1905 base and amendment and an unversioned WPS reference; WPS 2.0.10 records matching EasyMesh extensions. Profile-1 avoids requiring the full Profile-3 DPP onboarding path, but its actual 6.1 requirements must be applied.
scope: One virtual agent and one independently selected controller on isolated Ethernet
AP capability query/report for qualified represented resources
WSC M1/M2 for one existing fronthaul BSS only after full-radio scope is qualified
proposed_profile.proposed_security_scope: WPA2-Personal with AES, subject to actual pod representation and capabilities; no credentials, radio capabilities or trust properties are inferred from a schema
scope_constraints: Section 18 requires all mandatory functions for a claimed profile. This subset cannot claim complete Profile-1 conformance or certification.
Apply 6.1 profile/capability rules; do not import an older Profile-1 TLV list solely because the profile number matches.
WSC configures a complete radio BSS set (section 7.1). The one-BSS trial requires that the qualified radio has exactly that sole existing BSS, or a separately qualified complete-radio mapping.
The narrow trial cannot create/delete additional BSSs, tear down a radio, change backhaul or silently apply a convenient part of a larger request.
If full-radio ownership or any mandatory data cannot be proven, the affected provisioning/capability claim remains blocked.
Controller-triggered reconfiguration/renew requires its own procedure mapping if the chosen independent controller depends on it.

cross_cutting_sections.purpose: Normative dependencies, reliability, conditional fragmentation changes, processing order and profile requirements. Informative legacy-fragment note is not a replacement for normative framing rules.
Retrieve and verify base CMDU framing, fragmentation, reassembly and transmission/reception rules, including amendment effects.

procedures.name: AP autoconfiguration WSC M1/M2

timers.event: Controller replies to received M1 using the defined M2 configuration or teardown response
timers.meaning: Controller protocol response deadline; not confirmation of pod application.

verified_findings: A separate M1 exchange identifies each radio; its WSC MAC attribute uses the virtual 1905 AL MAC, not an assumed pod hardware MAC.
M2 processing validates the full radio configuration. Section 7.1 includes removal of existing BSSs that do not match any requested M2 configuration, and explicit radio teardown semantics.
WPS sections 7.1, 7.3 and 7.5 supply nonce/authenticator handling, key derivation and authenticated key wrapping. Tables 8, 9 and 20 and EasyMesh extensions must be interpreted together.
The candidate WPS edition explicitly reserves current EasyMesh extensions. It does not authorize substituting plaintext credentials or skipping authenticator verification.
Reject an unsupported overall semantic request before any pod write; map its wire behavior only after the IEEE/EasyMesh failure rules are verified.
remaining_gaps: IEEE WSC encapsulation, ordering, retry/duplicate and failure behavior require full normative review.
Independent M1/M2, key derivation, authenticator and key-wrap vectors are absent.
The one-BSS component patch has not been qualified as full-radio WSC semantics.
Hardware must establish sole-BSS radio scope or a complete supported mapping; shared management/backhaul dependencies and recovery remain unverified.
